propositions: The _CASCADING_EDGES table guarantees per-edge, same-edge parent movement only; §I4a's headline overstates this as a total-ordering constraint on parent-child status progression.

Two documented-intended residuals exist: (1) reactivating a closed child under an open parent does not cascade; (2) resuming a blocked child to in_progress under an open parent does not cascade despite the start-work gate firing.

The store enforces the operator-ruled invariant 'no non-terminal-state ticket can be a child of a closed ticket' jointly through the cascade table's two closed-source rows and the unconditional open-children close guard in transition_close.py.

The blocked-resume disagreement between the start-work gate (fires on blocked→in_progress) and the cascade table (omits that edge) must be resolved as non-cascading in docs and table comments, with reasoning that the gate and cascade answer different questions.

Narrowing §I4a to the per-edge guarantee, documenting both residuals with reasons, and resolving the blocked-resume disagreement requires rewording only; the cascade table rows, permission logic, and claim-status guard remain unchanged.
